type Profile = Pick<ReasoningConfiguration, 'sourceUrl' | 'basis'> & {
  configurations: Pick<ReasoningConfiguration, 'tier' | 'effort'>[];
};
const reasoningProfiles = profiles as Record<string, Profile>;

// Retain all configurations as evidence, including those disabled from the displayed roster.
export const initialModels: ModelRelease[] = modelCatalog.flatMap(model => {
  const profile = reasoningProfiles[model.id];
  return profile.configurations.map(config => ({
    ...model,
    id: config.tier === 'top' || config.tier === 'single' ? model.id : `${model.id}--${String(config.effort)}`,
    name: `${model.name} — ${config.effort ?? (model.isReasoningModel ? 'Effort not published' : 'Non-reasoning')}`,
    shortName: `${model.shortName} — ${config.effort ?? (model.isReasoningModel ? 'Effort not published' : 'Non-reasoning')}`,
    reasoningConfiguration: { ...config, releaseId: model.id, sourceUrl: profile.sourceUrl, basis: profile.basis }
  }));
});

// Disabled by request: less than 15% Real Frontier coverage on 2026-09-06.
export const enabledModels = initialModels.filter(model => !disabledConfigurations.includes(model.id));

const aaPerformanceObservations: MetricObservation[] = currentAAModels.flatMap((model) => {
  const observations: MetricObservation[] = [];

  if (model.outputSpeed !== undefined) {
    observations.push({
      modelId: model.modelId,
      metricId: 'output-speed',
      value: model.outputSpeed,
      observationDate: AA_OBSERVATION_DATE,
      sourceUrl: model.modelUrl
    });
  }
  if (model.taskTime !== undefined) {
    observations.push({
      modelId: model.modelId,
      metricId: 'time-per-task',
      value: model.taskTime,
      observationDate: AA_OBSERVATION_DATE,
      sourceUrl: model.modelUrl
    });
  }
  if (model.timeToFirstAnswerToken !== undefined) {
    observations.push({
      modelId: model.modelId,
      metricId: 'time-to-first-answer-token',
      value: model.timeToFirstAnswerToken,
      observationDate: AA_OBSERVATION_DATE,
      sourceUrl: model.modelUrl
    });
  }
  if (model.taskCost !== undefined) {
    observations.push({
      modelId: model.modelId,
      metricId: 'cost-per-task',
      value: model.taskCost,
      observationDate: AA_OBSERVATION_DATE,
      sourceUrl: model.modelUrl
    });
  }

  return observations;
});

# Fixed task basket for Real Index v1

The switch is feasible using AA's public evaluation data. SciCode's page explicitly publishes per-task output tokens split into reasoning and answer, per-task cost split into uncached input/cache reads/cache writes/reasoning/answer, and decode time. The page's public client dataset supplies the same canonical usage fields for other evaluations and exact model configurations.

Source: https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/scicode. The downloaded public page-data manifest path and decoded payload SHA-256 are recorded in task-benchmark-inputs-2026-09-07.json, along with the AA client calculation source URLs. The source's standard client decompression/decryption was used with its publicly delivered manifest. No account or paid API was used.

## Frozen workload

| Benchmark | Pinned definition | Tasks | Weight |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| SciCode | 1.0.1 | 288 | 20% |
| Humanity's Last Exam | AA text-only, no tools | 2,158 | 20% |
| AA-LCR | 1.1 | 100 | 20% |
| GDPval-AA | v2 | 220 | 20% |
| tau3-banking | AA banking configuration | 97 | 20% |

Source pages: https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/scicode, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/humanitys-last-exam, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/gdpval-aa, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/tau3-banking.

These established benchmarks provide scientific coding, reasoning, long-context synthesis, professional agentic work, and customer-service tool use. Continued upstream support is a judgment, not a guarantee. Benchmark versions, denominators, and weights are changed on our schedule. A future AA revision must be collected as a new explicit snapshot, not silently substituted into this basket.

## Billing and time

For non-agentic usage, AA prices input normally. For cacheable agentic usage, AA calculates cache reads as cacheable input times its published cache-hit rate, and cache writes as all input minus those reads. These are disjoint categories: uncached input is zero in that branch. Missing cache read/write prices use the regular input rate, matching AA. Fable's published per-evaluation fallback fractions price primary and fallback tokens separately by input, answer and reasoning share. No single-provider approximation replaces that billing mix.

Each cost component is divided by the pinned task count. Decode seconds are (reasoning + answer tokens) / task count / canonical answer throughput. This reproduces AA's per-evaluation time definition, which excludes TTFT, tool time and overhead. For example, Astra max SciCode reproduces 399.9826 answer tokens, 3,786.8194 reasoning tokens, $0.2322592 and 69.5615 decode seconds per task.

Aggregate cost, time and token quantities are arithmetic means with the fixed benchmark weights. Two available benchmarks qualify as full performance coverage; weights are renormalized over the available set. This can compare somewhat different workload subsets, a deliberate tradeoff authorized for performance. Actual membership is retained in the details. Intelligence coverage is unchanged.

## Coverage and estimates

Collected 260 benchmark token records over 52 exact native source configurations, including extra settings used only as paired references. The 57 displayed configurations receive 39 direct fixed-basket results and 15 lower-effort component estimates. All 54 resolved configurations currently have five contributing benchmarks. The September 2 Qwen3.8 Max refresh has no compatible source rows at any displayed setting; its three configurations remain enabled but without task-basket coverage. The earlier Qwen3.8 Max release is not substituted.

Missing lower efforts use same-release measured Top components and per-benchmark peer lower/Top ratios for the same exact effort transition. Target releases and Astra are excluded from donor fits. Unspecified effort is Top-only, preserving the assumption. Native usage remains separate from inferred usage. Held-out validation across 39 pairs gives median absolute error of 17.45% for cost and 23.24% for time with measured lower speed; missing-speed fallback uncertainty is not covered by that result.

The generated data retains per-benchmark and aggregate reasoning, answer and total output tokens for future scatter axes. No token normalization or quality score was invented, and no UI component or option was changed. Existing affordability weights remain 90% task cost / 10% 7:2:1 price; speed retains 78% task time / 12% first-answer latency / 10% output throughput. The proposed 20/60/20 price-blend design was superseded by this usage-preserving basket.

The best direct normalized task-cost scores span 12.52–100; task-time scores span 14.90–100. Both exceed the 15-point minimum spread. Existing normalization bounds remain fixed. All published index versions and public composite versions are 1.0.

Regenerate with `bun run performance:generate`, `bun run calibrate`, and `bun run sensitivity`. Source evidence is frozen in task-benchmark-inputs-2026-09-07.json; taskPerformance.json contains benchmark-level results and raw token quantities, and performanceEstimates.json contains the active estimates. The historical AA aggregate system remains in reports and release-level source observations; it cannot fill fixed-basket task gaps.

# Component-based task fallback, using Sol as the reference

## Current estimator after the audit

The deployed estimator now uses component peer ratios and measured lower-effort speed whenever available. It no longer blends latency changes into the component factors. Missing speed and latency still use peer ratios. This supersedes the hybrid deployment recommendation below; the earlier study remains recorded for context.

The generator compares three routes on the same 13 held-out native transitions from three releases, excluding the target release from every donor pool and fit. Median absolute task-time error is 26.1% for the old blend and 13.3% for peer components with measured speed; median cost error is 13.3% versus 6.6%. With speed also estimated, peer time error is 11.7%. These are distinct input conditions: a lower aggregate error when estimating speed is not a reason to discard measured speed in production. The small sample does not establish accuracy for every provider. Exact predictions and all three summaries are retained in performance-estimates-validation-2026-09-06.json.

Use separate reasoning, answer, uncached-input, cache-read and cache-write components. This supersedes the blended-cost proposal in performance-fallback-design-2026-09-06.md. Astra is excluded from this revised study's fitting, peer factors and validation at the user's request. The raw source snapshot retains it for provenance; no published observations or scores were removed.

Sol is the worked reference. Calibration still uses the other eligible releases rather than assuming every provider behaves like Sol. The revised study has 12 Top-to-lower pairs from five releases: Sol, Terra, Luna, Claude Opus 5 and Muse Spark 1.3. Each validation fold excludes the entire target release from fitting and peer ratios. Its measured Top remains available as the intended predictor anchor. Results are exploratory and lack an independent final test set.

## Sol's measured component spread

Weighted AA Intelligence Index quantities from the frozen September 6 snapshot:

| Native effort | Reasoning tokens/task | Answer tokens/task | Uncached input cost | Cache read cost | Cache write cost | Reasoning cost | Answer cost | Total cost | Decode time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| max | 14,121 | 8,620 | $0.0869 | $0.4952 | $0.2125 | $0.2824 | $0.1724 | $1.2495 | 271.5 s |
| xhigh | 8,061 | 7,246 | $0.0827 | $0.2983 | $0.2019 | $0.1612 | $0.1449 | $0.8891 | 189.9 s |
| high | 4,563 | 5,683 | $0.0816 | $0.1858 | $0.1421 | $0.0913 | $0.1137 | $0.6145 | 144.1 s |
| medium | 1,874 | 3,907 | $0.0816 | $0.0781 | $0.0919 | $0.0375 | $0.0781 | $0.3671 | 78.9 s |
| low | 668 | 2,487 | $0.0815 | $0.0288 | $0.0517 | $0.0134 | $0.0497 | $0.2251 | 43.4 s |

Sources: [Sol max](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-5-6-sol), [xhigh](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-5-6-sol-xhigh), [high](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-5-6-sol-high), [medium](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-5-6-sol-medium), [low](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/gpt-5-6-sol-low). The checked-in study inputs preserve the exact snapshot numbers, which can differ from a later rolling page update.

Uncached input is approximately stable, but reasoning is not the only large change. From max to low, reasoning tokens fall to 4.7%, answer tokens to 28.9%, cache-read cost to 5.8%, and cache-write cost to 24.3%. These are aggregate usage changes. They do not establish how many tools were called, which outputs were final prose versus tool messages, or whether higher effort made tool use more efficient.

Holding everything except reasoning fixed would predict Sol low at $0.9804 even with its actual reasoning count supplied. Its measured task cost is $0.2251. Sol therefore also supports estimating answer/cache usage separately.

## Cost calculation

Use disjoint components, avoiding double counting AA's aggregate `input` and `output` fields:

```
C = C_uncached + C_cacheRead + C_cacheWrite + C_reasoning + C_answer
```

When actual weighted billable usage and compatible rates exist:

```
C = (N_uncached*p_uncached + N_cacheRead*p_cacheRead
     + N_cacheWrite*p_cacheWrite + R*p_reasoning + A*p_answer) / 1e6
```

Prices are USD/million tokens. Use the provider's billing definitions for cache writes and distinct reasoning rates. With the same output rate for reasoning and answer, their last two terms reduce to `(R+A)*p_output`.

For missing lower-effort usage, fit each component separately. For native transition a→b, using the same paired releases in both means:

```
peer_j = mean(component_j,b) / mean(component_j,a)
x = (speed_b * firstAnswerLatency_b) / (speed_a * firstAnswerLatency_a)
factor_j = sqrt(peer_j * x^beta_j)
estimated component_j,b = component_j,a * factor_j
```

Fit each beta by release-weighted log-ratio regression through zero. Learn reasoning and answer token factors from their token counts. Learn disjoint cost-component factors from the directly published per-task component costs. Sum predicted component costs to produce the task-cost estimate. For the within-release pairs tested here, endpoint rates do not change with effort. Published component costs preserve their actual pricing mix; they are preferable to reverse-engineering token counts when a cache-write rate is missing.

If compatible component usage/rates are directly known for the target setting, use them and estimate only missing ingredients. Endpoint price availability alone does not establish per-task usage. The catalog's lower-effort rows missing task cost/time generally also lack weighted task token counts. The 2,000-token default used by AA's latency display is not weighted reasoning tokens per Intelligence Index task.

Known standalone versus fallback-assisted releases retain their distinction. For Fable's fallback-assisted runs, a single model's list output rate does not exactly reproduce the published output-cost component. Preserve the published component or actual multi-model billing mix rather than applying one rate to all output tokens.

## Time calculation and what it measures

[AA defines time per task](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models) as weighted decode time, excluding first-token latency and overhead. The app's existing metric should retain that definition:

```
estimated T_b = T_a
                * (estimated R_b + estimated A_b) / (R_a + A_a)
                * speed_a / speed_b
```

This preserves the measured Top relationship between token usage, throughput and task time. Direct `(R+A)/speed` reconstruction has about 6.1% median error on the non-Astra study rows, but substantial outliers; its 80th-percentile error is 45.2%. The Top anchor absorbs that measured mismatch without attributing it to unobserved tool calls. It does not prove the mismatch remains constant across settings, which is why held-out task prediction remains necessary.

If distinct reasoning and answer decoding speeds become available, estimate those durations separately. Do not add inclusive first-answer latency on top of a reasoning duration that already accounts for the same thinking.

A future wall-clock task metric would instead need sums over model calls and tool executions:

```
wallTime ≈ sum(per-call prefill/network time)
           + total reasoning decode time + total answer/tool-message decode time
           + tool execution and orchestration time
```

Parallel execution would require critical-path treatment. A 25-token tool message can be an explicit scenario assumption, but neither tool-call count nor tool execution time follows from AA's aggregate token counts. It should not be inserted into the existing AA decode-time fallback.

## Revised backtest, with Astra excluded

| Method | Median time error | Median cost error | 80th-percentile time error | 80th-percentile cost error |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Change only reasoning, supplying actual lower reasoning | 24.6% | 64.9% | 83.7% | 172.6% |
| Separate component peer ratios | 17.7% | 17.6% | 29.4% | 28.4% |
| Separate components, blending peer and measured latency/speed change | **12.9%** | **12.2%** | **25.2%** | **23.5%** |
| Same blend, but only 10% of non-reasoning adjustments | 18.5% | 60.9% | 100.4% | 163.0% |

The actual-reasoning row is a diagnostic, not a deployable fallback or fair feature-matched competitor. It shows that even perfect knowledge of lower reasoning cannot repair the assumption that all other components stay fixed.

The previous component study including Astra had hybrid medians of 13.2% time and 9.8% cost. Removing it leaves time accuracy similar and raises cost error to 12.2%. The broader component design remains useful; the earlier 9.8% claim does not describe the revised non-Astra pool.

The max→low and max→medium factors now each have only Sol and Opus as donors. A held-out fold consequently has one peer for those transitions. Treat the coefficients as provisional transfer estimates, not provider-independent laws. Sol is a concrete reference example, not proof that its curve should be copied across every model.

## Missing inputs and publication

If lower latency/speed are absent, use the component peer ratios alone. Do not treat peer-estimated timing as an independent measured signal in the geometric blend. Preserve the earlier distinction between a measured Top anchor and an estimated Top anchor; chained estimates need their own validation. If no Top component usage exists, a population or blended-price fallback remains a weaker route.

Keep all predictions in a separate performance estimate layer, with individual component provenance, native transition, donor releases and the Astra exclusion recorded. Do not turn inferred token counts into observations or use estimates to fit calibration. Direct measurements always win. A product integration would use the shared observation selector and preserve coherent provider/harness/snapshot bundles.

Implemented after user approval: 25 configurations receive task cost/time estimates, and 13 also receive missing speed/latency estimates. Direct observations are unchanged; speed and affordability scores now have complete coverage for 51/57 configurations. The existing publication dates already read 2026-09-06.

The shipped generator shares the reasoning/answer token factors with their corresponding output-cost factors. It excludes each target release from its donors and fits. Its validation covers the exact transitions needed by the 25 configurations, including high/xhigh anchors: 13 held-out pairs from three releases. Hybrid median absolute errors are 26.1% for time and 13.3% for cost; the peer-only route (also estimating speed) gives 11.7% time and 6.6% cost. These are different validation rows from the earlier 12-pair Top-only study above and should not be compared as if the sample were unchanged. Peer timing median errors are 5.4% speed and 35.7% latency. Full predictions and 80th-percentile errors are in performance-estimates-validation-2026-09-06.json.

Regenerate the shipped artifact with `bun run performance:generate`; the earlier Python study remains an exploratory comparison. Source evidence, factors and exact donor pairs are visible in the UI. No estimate enters the measurement pool.

Reproduce with `python3 scripts/studyComponentPerformanceFallbacks.py`. The resulting JSON includes every held-out prediction, Sol's full component table, fitted exponents, peer factors and donor releases.
